question: What was the main characteristic of the Indian economy at the time of independence in 1947?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Predominantly agrarian with low productivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Indian economy at the time of **independence in 1947** was predominantly **agrarian**. Agriculture contributed nearly **50% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** and employed a large majority of the population.
 
• Agriculture was characterized by **low productivity**, primarily due to **traditional farming methods**, lack of modern inputs such as fertilizers, irrigation facilities, and dependence on monsoons.
 
• Land distribution was highly unequal, with a large number of peasants working as **tenants, sharecroppers, or landless laborers** under exploitative conditions. This led to widespread poverty and low living standards.
 
• The industrial sector was **underdeveloped**, contributing only a small share to the GDP. The economy lacked a significant manufacturing base, and most industries were limited to **primary processing** rather than production of finished goods.
